name: Single-agent Cisplatin Concurrent with Radiation (Vaginal SCC Chemoradiation)

biomarkers.note: Single-agent cisplatin as a radiosensitizer is not biomarker gated. PD-L1 and TMB-H/MSI-H are tested to guide later immunotherapy in advanced/recurrent disease, not this chemoradiation.

lineOfTherapy: primary (definitive) treatment of locally advanced primary vaginal SCC; radiosensitizing chemotherapy concurrent with external-beam radiation plus brachytherapy

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: locally advanced primary vaginal squamous cell carcinoma treated with concurrent chemoradiation
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v2.2026, Systemic Therapy for Primary Vaginal Cancer (VAG-D 1 of 2), Chemoradiation: Cisplatin (Carboplatin if cisplatin intolerant); footnote (Concurrent platinum-containing chemotherapy with EBRT utilizes cisplatin as a single agent, or carboplatin if cisplatin intolerant)

drugs.name: CISplatin

provenance.locator: VAG-D 1 of 2, Chemoradiation: Cisplatin (Carboplatin if patient is cisplatin intolerant); regimen named but per-dose number not printed

drugs.notes: Single-agent CISplatin is the radiosensitizing chemotherapy given concurrently with EBRT plus brachytherapy for locally advanced primary vaginal SCC (NCCN Vaginal v2.2026, VAG-D). The cited source names the regimen (concurrent platinum-based chemoradiation improves outcomes and is often used in stage II to IV disease) but does NOT print the cisplatin dose, basis, unit, or schedule; all set to VERIFY. For clinical context only (not asserted here as the vaginal dose): the analogous cervical radiosensitizing schedule is weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m2 (DeVita line 170910). Requires hydration and nephro/oto/neuro monitoring; carboplatin substitutes if cisplatin intolerant. Tall man per ISMP.

premedications.name: Cisplatin hydration and antiemetics
premedications.notes: IV hydration before and after cisplatin; antiemetic prophylaxis for the platinum agent.

supportiveCare: cisplatin hydration protocol (pre- and post-infusion) to reduce nephrotoxicity.
management of additive chemoradiation acute toxicity (vaginal, GU/GI mucosa).

monitoring: renal function (creatinine, electrolytes/Mg) before each dose
audiometry/otologic and peripheral-neuropathy assessment for cisplatin
weekly review of concurrent radiation acute toxicity

doseModificationRules.condition: rising creatinine, electrolyte derangement, or grade 2+ cisplatin toxicity
doseModificationRules.text: Hold cisplatin or switch to carboplatin if cisplatin intolerant per NCCN; physician decides.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: Vaginal cancer management: definitive concurrent chemoradiation (platinum-based) plus brachytherapy for locally advanced disease (Chapter 49, vaginal carcinoma); the systemic chemotherapy dose is not tabulated

guideline.locator: Systemic Therapy for Primary Vaginal Cancer (VAG-D 1 of 2), Chemoradiation: Cisplatin (Carboplatin if cisplatin intolerant); primary-treatment footnotes (concurrent platinum-based chemotherapy improves outcomes, often used in stage II to IV)

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for single-agent cisplatin concurrent with radiation for locally advanced primary vaginal squamous cell carcinoma (StewardMD subtype #49; no dedicated vaginal_cancer reference disease exists, so diseaseId is null). The regimen identity and curative concurrent-chemoradiation setting are grounded to Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Vaginal Cancer v2.2026 (VAG-D 1 of 2, Chemoradiation: single-agent Cisplatin, or Carboplatin if cisplatin intolerant; concurrent platinum-based chemoradiation improves outcomes in stage II to IV). However, the cited source does NOT print the cisplatin dose, basis, unit, schedule, or cycle count; therefore cisplatin basis/dosePerUnit/unit/days plus cycleLengthDays and cycles are set to VERIFY and listed in verifyFields, pending a dosing source. No dose was invented or inferred (the weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m2 cervical radiosensitizing schedule is cited only as clinical context for the verifier). Cisplatin requires hydration with nephro-, oto-, and neurotoxicity monitoring. Tall man per ISMP. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
